name: Dental Implants
description: Permanent, natural-looking replacements for missing teeth, anchored securely in the jawbone.
content: A dental implant is a small titanium post placed in the jawbone that acts as an artificial root. Once it integrates with the bone, a custom crown is attached — restoring the look, feel and chewing strength of a natural tooth. Implants also help preserve bone and keep neighbouring teeth from drifting.
benefits: Looks and feels like a natural tooth
No need to grind down adjacent teeth
Can last decades with good care
whoNeedsIt: Adults missing one or more teeth
Those with adequate bone density (or suitable for grafting)

procedure.title: Consultation & 3D planning
procedure.description: Clinical exam, CBCT scan and a written treatment plan with costs.

procedure.title: Implant placement
procedure.description: A short, comfortable procedure under local anaesthesia.

procedure.title: Healing (osseointegration)
procedure.description: Typically 8–12 weeks while the implant fuses with bone.

procedure.title: Final crown
procedure.description: A custom-shaded crown is fitted and your bite is fine-tuned.

recovery: Mild soreness for 2–3 days is normal and managed with standard pain relief. Soft foods are advised for the first week. Most patients return to work the next day.

faqs.question: Is implant surgery painful?
faqs.answer: It is done under local anaesthesia and most patients describe it as easier than an extraction.

faqs.question: How long do implants last?
faqs.answer: With good oral hygiene and regular check-ups, implants can last 20 years or more.

name: Root Canal Treatment
description: Save an infected or painful tooth with precise, comfortable rotary root canal therapy.
content: Root canal treatment removes infected or inflamed pulp from inside the tooth, disinfects the canals and seals them. Using rotary instruments and apex locators, most treatments are completed in one or two visits with minimal discomfort.
whoNeedsIt: Sensitivity to hot or cold that doesn't settle
A swollen gum or abscess near a tooth

procedure.title: Diagnosis & X-ray
procedure.description: We confirm the cause and map the canals digitally.

procedure.title: Cleaning & shaping
procedure.description: Infected pulp is removed and canals are disinfected.

procedure.title: Sealing
procedure.description: Canals are filled and sealed with biocompatible material.

procedure.title: Crown
procedure.description: A crown is usually recommended to protect the treated tooth.

recovery: Tenderness when biting may last a few days. Avoid chewing hard foods on the tooth until the final crown is placed.

faqs.question: Does a root canal hurt?
faqs.answer: Modern anaesthesia makes it comparable to getting a filling. It relieves pain rather than causing it.

faqs.question: Do I need a crown afterwards?
faqs.answer: For back teeth, a crown is strongly recommended to prevent fracture.

name: Teeth Whitening
description: Professional in-clinic whitening that lifts stains safely — several shades brighter in one visit.
content: Our in-clinic whitening uses a professional-grade gel activated under controlled conditions, with gums fully protected. It is safe for enamel and delivers far more predictable results than over-the-counter kits.
benefits: Visible results in a single session
whoNeedsIt: Stains from tea, coffee or tobacco
Anyone preparing for a special occasion

procedure.title: Shade assessment
procedure.description: We record your starting shade and check for sensitivity.

procedure.title: Gum protection
procedure.description: A protective barrier is applied to your gums.

procedure.title: Whitening sessions
procedure.description: Gel is applied in timed cycles for even results.

procedure.title: Aftercare
procedure.description: Desensitising treatment and diet advice for 48 hours.

recovery: Mild sensitivity for 24–48 hours is common. Avoid strongly coloured food and drinks for two days.

faqs.question: How long do results last?
faqs.answer: Typically 12–24 months, depending on diet and habits.

faqs.question: Will whitening work on crowns?
faqs.answer: No — whitening only affects natural enamel. We'll plan around existing restorations.

name: Crowns & Bridges
description: Durable ceramic and zirconia crowns that restore strength and appearance to damaged teeth.
content: Crowns cover and protect weakened teeth, while bridges replace a missing tooth by anchoring to neighbouring teeth. We use digital impressions and high-strength ceramics for accurate fit and natural shading.

procedure.title: Tooth preparation
procedure.description: The tooth is shaped to make room for the crown.

procedure.title: Digital scan
procedure.description: An intraoral scan captures a precise model.

procedure.title: Temporary crown
procedure.description: Protects the tooth while the lab crafts your crown.

procedure.title: Fitting
procedure.description: The final crown is checked, adjusted and cemented.

recovery: Slight gum tenderness for a day or two. Normal eating can resume once the final crown is fitted.

faqs.question: Zirconia or porcelain?
faqs.answer: Zirconia is stronger for back teeth; layered ceramics offer the best aesthetics at the front.

name: Porcelain Veneers
description: Ultra-thin ceramic shells that transform the shape, colour and alignment of front teeth.
content: Veneers are custom-made porcelain shells bonded to the front surface of teeth. They correct chips, gaps, discolouration and minor misalignment with minimal tooth reduction.
whoNeedsIt: Deep stains that don't respond to whitening

procedure.title: Smile design
procedure.description: Digital preview of your new smile before any work begins.

procedure.title: Preparation
procedure.description: A thin layer of enamel is refined.

procedure.title: Bonding
procedure.description: Veneers are bonded and polished.

recovery: No downtime. Some patients notice brief sensitivity after preparation.

faqs.question: How many veneers do I need?
faqs.answer: Most smile designs involve 6–10 upper teeth, but it depends on your smile line.

name: Clear Aligners
description: Nearly invisible, removable aligners to straighten teeth without brackets or wires.
content: Clear aligners gradually move teeth using a series of custom trays planned digitally. They're removable for eating and brushing, and practically invisible in daily life.
benefits: Digital preview of your final result

procedure.title: Scan & plan
procedure.description: 3D scan and a digital simulation of tooth movement.

procedure.title: Aligner series
procedure.description: Switch to a new set every 1–2 weeks.

procedure.title: Progress checks
procedure.description: Short reviews every 6–8 weeks.

procedure.title: Retention
procedure.description: Retainers keep your new smile in place.

recovery: Each new set may feel tight for a day or two — a sign they're working.

faqs.question: How many hours a day?
faqs.answer: Aligners should be worn 20–22 hours daily for predictable results.

name: Metal & Ceramic Braces
description: Reliable fixed orthodontics for teens and adults, with tooth-coloured ceramic options.
content: Fixed braces remain the most versatile option for correcting complex crowding and bite problems. Ceramic brackets offer a discreet alternative to traditional metal.
whoNeedsIt: Teens with crowding or bite issues

procedure.title: Records
procedure.description: Photos, X-rays and models for planning.

procedure.title: Bonding
procedure.description: Brackets are attached and wires placed.

procedure.title: Adjustments
procedure.description: Monthly visits to progress treatment.

recovery: Mild soreness for a few days after placement and adjustments.

name: Scaling & Polishing
description: Thorough professional cleaning to remove plaque and tartar and keep gums healthy.
content: Professional scaling removes hardened tartar that brushing cannot, followed by polishing to smooth the tooth surface and reduce future build-up.

procedure.title: Examination
procedure.description: Gum health check and charting.

procedure.title: Ultrasonic scaling
procedure.description: Gentle removal of tartar.

procedure.title: Polishing
procedure.description: Smooths enamel and removes stains.

recovery: No downtime. Slight gum sensitivity for a day is normal.

faqs.question: Does cleaning damage enamel?
faqs.answer: No. Professional scaling removes deposits, not enamel.

name: Tooth-Coloured Fillings
description: Invisible composite fillings that repair cavities and blend seamlessly with your teeth.
content: Composite fillings are bonded directly to the tooth, requiring less drilling than metal fillings and matching the natural shade of your teeth.

procedure.title: Decay removal
procedure.description: Affected tooth structure is removed gently.

procedure.title: Layering
procedure.description: Composite is placed in thin, cured layers.

procedure.title: Shaping & polish
procedure.description: Bite adjusted and surface polished.

recovery: You can eat normally once numbness wears off.

name: Tooth Extraction
description: Gentle, atraumatic removal of damaged or non-restorable teeth.
content: When a tooth cannot be saved, we perform atraumatic extractions that protect surrounding bone — important if you plan to replace it with an implant later.

procedure.title: Assessment
procedure.description: X-ray and discussion of replacement options.

procedure.title: Extraction
procedure.description: Performed under local anaesthesia.

procedure.title: Aftercare
procedure.description: Written instructions and a follow-up check.

recovery: Avoid rinsing, straws and smoking for 24 hours. Most discomfort settles within 2–3 days.

faqs.question: Should I replace an extracted tooth?
faqs.answer: Usually yes — gaps can cause neighbouring teeth to shift.

name: Wisdom Tooth Removal
description: Safe surgical removal of impacted or painful wisdom teeth.
content: Impacted wisdom teeth can cause pain, infection and damage to adjacent teeth. We plan each case with digital imaging for a safe, efficient procedure.
whoNeedsIt: Pain or swelling at the back of the mouth
Recurrent gum infection around wisdom teeth

procedure.title: Imaging
procedure.description: OPG or CBCT to assess position and nerves.

procedure.title: Surgery
procedure.description: Performed under local anaesthesia.

procedure.title: Review
procedure.description: Suture check after one week.

recovery: Expect swelling for 2–4 days. Cold compresses and soft foods help. Most patients take one or two days off.

faqs.question: Do all wisdom teeth need removal?
faqs.answer: No — only those causing problems or likely to.

name: Children's Dentistry
description: Friendly, preventive dental care that helps children build healthy habits early.
content: Our child-friendly appointments focus on prevention — fluoride application, pit-and-fissure sealants and gentle treatment — in an environment designed to make kids feel at ease.

procedure.title: Tell-show-do
procedure.description: We explain every step in child-friendly language.

procedure.title: Check-up
procedure.description: Gentle exam and cleaning.

procedure.title: Prevention
procedure.description: Fluoride or sealants as needed.

faqs.question: When should my child first visit?
faqs.answer: By their first birthday or when the first tooth appears.

name: Gum Disease Treatment
description: Deep cleaning and periodontal care to treat bleeding, receding or infected gums.
content: Gum disease is the leading cause of tooth loss in adults. Deep cleaning (root planing) removes bacteria below the gumline and allows gums to heal and reattach.

procedure.title: Charting
procedure.description: Pocket depths measured around every tooth.

procedure.title: Deep cleaning
procedure.description: Root surfaces cleaned under anaesthesia.

procedure.title: Maintenance
procedure.description: Review in 6–8 weeks.

recovery: Gums may be tender for a few days. Warm salt-water rinses help healing.

faqs.question: Is gum disease reversible?
faqs.answer: Early gingivitis is fully reversible; periodontitis can be controlled.

name: Complete & Partial Dentures
description: Comfortable, natural-looking dentures designed for a secure fit and confident smile.
content: Modern dentures are custom-designed for comfort and appearance. Implant-supported options offer significantly better stability.

procedure.title: Impressions
procedure.description: Detailed moulds of your gums.

procedure.title: Try-in
procedure.description: Preview fit, bite and appearance.

procedure.title: Delivery
procedure.description: Final fit with adjustments.

recovery: An adjustment period of 2–4 weeks is normal.

faqs.question: Can I sleep with dentures?
faqs.answer: We recommend removing them at night to let gums rest.

name: Smile Makeover
description: A personalised combination of cosmetic treatments to redesign your smile.
content: A smile makeover combines whitening, veneers, contouring and alignment to achieve your ideal smile — planned digitally so you can preview the result first.

procedure.title: Smile design
procedure.description: Photos, scans and a digital mock-up.

procedure.title: Treatment phases
procedure.description: Sequenced whitening, veneers or aligners.

procedure.title: Finishing
procedure.description: Final polish and maintenance plan.

faqs.question: How long does a makeover take?
faqs.answer: From two weeks to several months, depending on the plan.

name: Consultation & Digital X-Ray
description: A thorough examination with digital X-rays and a clear, written treatment plan.
content: Every journey at SmileCare begins with a full consultation: oral examination, digital X-rays where needed, and an honest conversation about your options and costs.

procedure.title: History
procedure.description: Medical and dental history review.

procedure.title: Examination
procedure.description: Teeth, gums, bite and soft tissues.

procedure.title: Plan
procedure.description: Options, timelines and costs explained.

faqs.question: Is the consultation fee adjusted?
faqs.answer: Yes — it's adjusted against treatment started within 30 days.
